anchor_commit_observation.message:
fix(client): restore mdiConsoleLine import + add chrome ErrorBoundary

Spawning a new session in the Electron app blanked the entire window
(incl. titlebar, app frozen) until reload. Root cause: commit 26cc9ee7
removed mdiConsoleLine from the @mdi/js import in SessionCard.tsx but
left two `?? mdiConsoleLine` fallbacks behind. Existing sessions all
carry known sources, so the dangling reference stayed cold; a freshly
spawned session with a source missing from sourceIcons evaluated the
fallback and threw `ReferenceError: mdiConsoleLine is not defined`
during render. The throw bubbled past the layout chrome (no
ErrorBoundary above the inner ChatView one at App.tsx:1117), unmounting
the entire React tree.

Three layers of fix:

1. Restore the missing import in SessionCard.tsx (one-line).
2. Wrap apiProvider's children in a top-level <ErrorBoundary> so any
   future render-time throw in chrome (sidebar, session list, content
   header, MobileShell) degrades to a recoverable 'Shell encountered an
   error' panel + Reload button instead of blanking the window. Inner
   ChatView boundary still wins for chat-only errors via React's
   nearest-boundary semantics.
3. Repo-lint no-undeclared-mdi-fallback.test.ts: scan client .tsx for
   `?? mdi<Name>` fallbacks and assert each identifier is in an
   `import { ... } from '@mdi/js'` in the same file. Closes the gap
   that let this regression ship (Vite does not enforce tsc's
   undeclared-name check at bundle time).

Tests: shell-error-boundary.test.tsx pins the boundary contract
(testid `shell-error-fallback`); no-undeclared-mdi-fallback verified
to fail on a deliberate dangling fallback and pass after restore.
5292 tests green.

Archived as 2026-05-09-fix-session-card-icon-import-and-shell-boundary.
New main spec: client-shell-error-isolation (2 ADDED requirements,
5 scenarios).

commits.message:
Fix API base URL, correct field names, add e2e tests

Major discovery: the Watermelon API uses /api/v1 prefix (not /),
and field names differ from what was assumed (email_address not email,
first_name/last_name not name, etc). Webhook API uses action_id/
entity_id/verb_id (not event strings) and doesn't support GET listing.

- Fix BASE_URL to https://public.watermelon.ai/api/v1
- Rewrite contacts tools: email_address (required), first_name,
  last_name, telephone_number, location
- Rewrite search: fieldValue + optional fieldId (not query string)
- Rewrite webhooks: action_id/entity_id/verb_id params, remove
  nonexistent list endpoint
- Rewrite messages: payload field, user_id param
- Add Field() validators for schema-visible bounds
- Improve all tool docstrings for LLM self-description
- Add e2e test suite: 12 tests (10 pass, 2 skip for conversations
  which need a chatbot configured)
- Handle API response shapes (list wrapping, 204 no-content)

Initial commit: MCP server for Watermelon.ai (13 tools)

TypeScript MCP server wrapping the full Watermelon public API:
contacts (5), conversations (2), messages (2), fields (1), webhooks (3).
Includes gap analysis and OpenSpec artifacts.

feat(ci): CI wait mode + cancel-stale-review + skills doc (#1)

Adds opt-in CI wait mode so the bot defers review until the GitLab pipeline
for the reviewed commit passes, plus fixes for the multi-pipeline and
re-push races that the new mode surfaces. Also adds the daily-workflow
skills doc and an in-flight coordinator that cancels a stale review when a
newer push arrives.

## Features

- ci.require (opt-in via .pi/config.yaml): bot waits for CI success before
  reviewing, listens to pipeline webhooks, and skips review on failed/
  canceled/ skipped pipelines. Per-project ci.waitTimeoutMs overrides the
  CI_WAIT_TIMEOUT_MS env default.
- Pipeline webhook handler in index.ts consumes pending entries keyed by
  projectId:sha to trigger deferred reviews.

## Bug fixes

- BUG 1 (stale CI wait on re-push): secondary mrIid->sha index in ciwait.ts
  clears the previous pending entry when a new push arrives, so a pipeline
  webhook for the old SHA can no longer trigger a stale review.
- BUG 2 (multi-pipeline aggregate): getMrPipelineStatus now filters
  pipelines by SHA and aggregates status across all of them (any running
  wins, all-success required), so a failing branch pipeline is no longer
  masked by a successful MR pipeline.
- BUG 3 (two reviews racing on re-push): new inflight.ts registers each
  review by projectId:mrIid and aborts the previous session via
  AbortSignal when a newer push supersedes it; performReview swallows the
  AbortError silently so the newer review owns the verdict.

## UX

- checkCiAndWait de-duplicates the 'Đợi CI pass' note per SHA via
  listMrComments, avoiding note spam when devs push repeatedly while CI is
  running.

## Observability

- /healthz and /stats expose ciWait.pending and reviewsActive counts.

## Docs

- docs/SKILLS.md: daily workflow skills for developers/AI agents using a
  project that already has the bot set up (read notes, decode verdicts,
  re-trigger, debug 'bot im lặng').
- docs/CONFIG.md, INTEGRATION.md, SETUP.md, ARCHITECTURE.md,
  MULTIPROJECT.md, AGENTS.md, README.md: document the ci schema, re-push
  behavior, D10/D11 decisions, and link cross-repo references to GitHub
  URLs.
- All doc references converted to absolute GitHub URLs.

## Tests

- 65 tests pass (was 22). Adds regressions for mergeConfig ci.* fields,
  resolveCiWaitTimeoutMs priority, ciwait pending lifecycle (incl. BUG 1
  re-push clear), aggregatePipelineStatus multi-pipeline cases (BUG 2),
  and inflight coordinator lifecycle (BUG 3).

Co-authored-by: Nai Coi <naicoi@gmail.com>

Bag-list thumbnails + archive add-bean-base-integration (#1437)

* Bag-list thumbnails + archive add-bean-base-integration

BagCard gains a 44px bag-photo thumbnail from the canonical snapshot blob
(same source and pattern as BeanBaseDetailsRow: PreserveAspectCrop,
async, thumbnail-resolution sourceSize) with a dimmed beans-icon
placeholder so imageless bags keep the row shape.

Archive add-bean-base-integration: everything else open was obsoleted by
the June keyless-canonical migration (#1336) — tasks annotated with why;
the settings-cloud-credentials delta (removed API-key UI, never in
production) deleted rather than promoted; stale key/two-stage-fetch
claims trimmed from bean-base-search; the unbuilt key-triggered dedup
requirement dropped from visualizer-bag-linkage so only shipped behavior
is promoted. Archived via `openspec archive`.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* Resolve bag photos via og:image into a file cache (never the DB)

The canonical DB has no image column, so the thumbnail/popup images were
sourcing an always-empty blob field. BeanBaseClient::ensureBagImage() now
resolves photos best-effort: product page (the canonical `url`, newly
captured into the blob as `link` — also reviving the popup's open-page
button) -> og:image meta tag -> downloaded to a size-capped LRU file
cache under CacheLocation/bagimages keyed by canonical id. Pixels never
enter the database; blobs linked before `link` was captured recover the
URL by re-searching the canonical API by name. One attempt per id per
session, silent on failure, file writes + eviction off the main thread.

BagCard and BeanBaseDetailsPopup read the cache (legacy blob `image`
kept as fallback); ChangeBeansDialog warms the cache at pick time.
Tests: og:image extraction variants, full resolve-and-cache chain
against the fake server, silent-failure dedup.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* Review fixes + product URL in the bag details popup

Review findings: atomic image writes (temp file + verified write + rename
— a truncated write could otherwise permanently satisfy the cache check
and suppress re-resolution), canonical-id filename sanitization (blocks
traversal via crafted blob ids from backups/migration), eviction only
credits successful removals, qWarning on local disk faults (expected
network misses stay silent), "LRU" wording corrected to oldest-written
eviction (verified the QDir::Time|Reversed direction against Qt source —
the reviewer's claim it was inverted was wrong), stale blob-era comments
fixed, and tests for the direct-productUrl path, hostile og:image
schemes, og:image:width anchoring, re-emit payload, and unsafe-id
rejection.

Feature: the details popup now shows the product URL itself under "View
at roaster" (reordering aid), and when the image re-search recovers a
URL for a pre-capture blob, bagLinkRecovered lets BagCard backfill it
into the bag blob (bag row only; shot snapshots stay as recorded).

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* Decouple reorder-link recovery from image resolution

The link backfill only ran inside the image re-search, so a bag whose
photo was already cached (Jeff's exact repro) never recovered its URL
and the popup's reorder row stayed hidden. recoverBagLink() is now its
own operation with its own per-session guard — BagCard requests it
whenever a linked blob lacks `link`, regardless of image state — and
ensureBagImage's legacy branch routes through it (a pending image
resolution continues from the recovered URL). Test pins the
cached-image + link-recovery combination.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

feat(files): image upload/serving with storage port/adapter

Implement the standalone tenant-scoped `files` bounded context:

- Storage port/adapter seam (IFileStoragePort + DatabaseFileStorageAdapter
  over Postgres bytea) so the backend can be swapped for S3/MinIO via a
  useClass rebind, with no domain/application/transport changes.
- Multipart REST upload (POST /files) + byte-serving download
  (GET /files/:id/content); list/metadata/delete REST endpoints.
- GraphQL read + delete; MCP tools file_find_by_id/file_list/file_delete.
- Image-only MIME allowlist (jpeg/png/webp), configurable max size (10MB),
  tenant isolation via createTenantRepository.
- Migration 1780000000019: files + file_contents (bytea, FK ON DELETE CASCADE).
- Unit + integration + e2e tests; FilesModule registered in AppModule.

Add SvelteKit frontend scaffold and CI

Introduce a full SvelteKit frontend scaffold and integrate frontend build/test pipelines into the repo. Adds frontend/ source, package.json and lockfile, Playwright E2E and accessibility tests, Playwright configs, and test helpers. Add GitHub Actions workflows for Playwright and accessibility runs, and enable Dependabot updates for the frontend npm workspace. Update dockerfile.www to perform a multi-stage build (build frontend static assets and copy into Python runtime), adjust .dockerignore and Prettier ignores, and add docs (docs/dev/frontend.md, docker.md, README links) and local frontend config files. Minor backend wiring and tests updated so the web server can serve the built SPA and CI artifacts are uploaded.

commits.message:
Fix gitignore: remove lib/ rule that was hiding frontend/src/lib/ from git

The Python packaging-convention 'lib/' pattern in .gitignore matched
frontend/src/lib/ and silently excluded the entire SvelteKit source lib
directory — all API clients, stores, components, and tests — from version
control. CI was failing with UNLOADABLE_DEPENDENCY errors because the
build had no access to any of these files.

Replaced the bare 'lib/' glob with a comment explaining why it was removed.
All frontend/src/lib/ files are now tracked.

* refactor(pagination): implement decorator pattern for Pageable translation

Refactors Pageable translation to use Decorator pattern instead of separate utility class.

Changes:
- Created TranslatedPageable decorator with static translate() method
  - Uses Decorator pattern: wraps Pageable with translated sort orders
  - API: TranslatedPageable.translate(original, translationMap)
  - Replaces PageableSortTranslator utility class
- Removed EventSortTranslator from EventController (unnecessary identity mapping)
  - JSON DTO fields match domain properties exactly
  - Simplified controller to pass Pageable directly to service layer
- Updated EventRepositoryAdapter to use TranslatedPageable.translate()
- Added comprehensive unit tests (8 test cases)
  - Single sort property translation
  - Multiple sort orders
  - Unknown property fallback (fail-safe)
  - Null handling preservation
  - Empty sort handling
  - Pagination parameters preservation
  - Pageable navigation methods (next, previous, first)
  - Type checking

Benefits:
- Cleaner API: TranslatedPageable.translate(pageable, map) vs PageableSortTranslator.translate()
- Better pattern alignment: Decorator pattern for wrapper functionality
- Single responsibility: TranslatedPageable handles both wrapping and translation
- Reduced duplication: 110 lines of duplicate PageableRequest removed
- Better testability: 8 focused unit tests for translation logic

feat: added sandbox environment (#687)

* feat(api): replace mongo VFS with JuiceFS-backed E2B sandbox

Rip out the mongo-based virtual filesystem and code_exec_tool; replace with
a persistent E2B sandbox per user whose /workspace is a JuiceFS bind-mount
backed by R2 + sharded postgres metadata. New coding tools (bash/read/write/
edit) operate inside the sandbox. Includes sandbox lifecycle pool, shard
router, mount script with ephemeral-fallback, build_e2b_template builder,
one-shot VFS→JuiceFS migration script, dev smoke-test endpoints, and the
compaction/summarization middleware rewrite to match the new tool surface.

* fix: hmr issue

* fix(api): make JuiceFS+R2 sandbox path actually work end-to-end

Validation against real R2 + Neon Postgres + E2B sandbox surfaced four
issues — fixing them all in one pass:

- shard_router: rewrite `postgresql://` -> `postgres://` since JuiceFS
  rejects the long scheme. Managed PG providers (Neon, Supabase) hand
  out the former.
- bootstrap: drop `--shards` from format (it requires a `%d` per-shard
  bucket URL placeholder we don't use) and drop `--encrypt-rsa-key`
  (the PEM overflows JuiceFS's varchar(4096) settings column). Strip
  whitespace from R2 creds before passing.
- lifecycle: strip R2 creds in sandbox envs; sudo --preserve-env so the
  mount script actually sees USER_ID and JFS_* env vars; _run_silent
  helper so `mountpoint -q` returning 1 stops raising; health probe
  before reusing a pooled sandbox so stale handles get evicted instead
  of hanging the next call for 60s.
- mount_juicefs.sh: chmod 0777 instead of chown on the bind-mounted
  JuiceFS path — chown doesn't always stick on FUSE, and per-user
  isolation already happens at the JuiceFS-path layer.

Verified end-to-end: bash tool writes /workspace/marker.txt in sandbox
A; sandbox A killed in E2B + cached doc cleared; sandbox B (fresh)
mounts JuiceFS against the same Neon+R2 backing store and reads the
marker back unchanged.

* fix(api): handle sslmode in asyncpg URL to fix Neon/Supabase connections

asyncpg rejects the `sslmode` query param that managed Postgres providers like Neon include in connection URLs. Strip it from the URL and translate it into a `connect_args` ssl value instead.

* feat(api,web): workspace v2 — per-session FS, uploads, artifact streaming

Replace the shared /workspace root with per-conversation sessions on
JuiceFS. Adds session lifecycle (create on chat start, delete on
conversation delete, daily prune), a per-sandbox artifact watcher that
streams .user-visible/ changes to the chat UI via Redis, host-side upload
mirroring into read-only user-uploaded/, /sessions HTTP endpoints to serve
artifacts, and inline artifact rendering on the web. Centralizes the
artifact-event wire contract and splits storage into juicefs/sessions.

* docs(api): align agent prompts with workspace v2

Add a CODING WORKSPACE section to the executor prompt: real durable
per-session filesystem, cwd = session root, scratch/ + read-only
user-uploaded/ + .user-visible/, and that bash is the primary capable
tool (read/write/edit are convenience wrappers). Replace stale "VFS" /
"virtual filesystem" terminology across executor, subagent, spawn, and
memory prompts.

* fix(api): correct artifact session keying + accesslog path; dockerize backend

E2E surfaced two real workspace-v2 defects:

- get_session_id() used the executor's ephemeral thread_id
  (executor_<conv>_<hex>) so coding tools wrote to a different session dir
  than ensure_session_dirs/the chat artifact forwarder keyed on, dropping
  every artifact event. Prefer vfs_session_id (subagent_runner pins it to
  the parent conversation thread for exactly this reason).
- accesslog watcher tailed /workspace/.accesslog, but JuiceFS exposes the
  accesslog only at the mount root (/mnt/jfs/.accesslog; /workspace is a
  bind-mount of the users/<uid> subdir) and it is root-owned — tail now
  targets the correct path with sudo -n.

* fix(api): make JuiceFS host mount reliable + non-blocking (prod-manageable)

internal 10s readiness self-check FATALs under managed-Postgres (Neon)
meta latency, and serverless cold-starts / transient DNS(AAAA) blips
killed the one-shot attempt.

bootstrap.py now:
- runs juicefs mount in the foreground as a detached child and polls the
  mountpoint itself (no reliance on the aggressive --background self-check)
- retries format+mount with exponential backoff on transient meta/network
  errors (Neon cold-start, DNS flap, blips)
- runs in a daemon thread so app startup is never blocked — storage
  helpers already soft-fail until /mnt/jfs converges
- is idempotent, never raises, logs structured progress, and is tunable
  via JUICEFS_MOUNT_READY_TIMEOUT / _BOOTSTRAP_MAX_ATTEMPTS /
  _BOOTSTRAP_RETRY_BACKOFF (no code change to tune in prod)

* fix(api): install arch-native juicefs (multi-arch image)

Silicon dev, Graviton prod) that runs under Rosetta/QEMU and crashes with
a Go runtime abort in the JuiceFS Postgres meta client, so the host-side
/mnt/jfs sidecar never mounts reliably. Use BuildKit's TARGETARCH so the
native amd64/arm64 binary is installed for the build platform.

* fix(api): retry juicefs mount crashes (allowlist-permanent classification)

juicefs intermittently aborts (Go runtime crash in the Neon meta
NewSession) — a register dump, not a tidy error string — so the
substring-based transient check misfiled it as fatal and bootstrap gave
up, even though the same meta mounts cleanly on a later attempt.

Invert the heuristic: only an explicit permanent error (auth, bucket,
bad host, cert) is fatal; everything else — network blips, Neon
cold-starts, opaque crashes — retries with backoff. Truncate the mount
log per attempt so classification reflects only the current try. Bump
defaults to 8 attempts / 3s base backoff (cap 30s).

* fix(api): resilient JuiceFS meta DNS (Docker embedded-DNS flakiness)

Real root cause of the flaky host mount: Docker's embedded resolver
(127.0.0.11) intermittently returns "no such host" for the external Neon
meta host on rapid back-to-back lookups (juicefs status resolves, mount
3ms later fails). It is not a crash/Rosetta/perms.

- dns_opt attempts:5 timeout:3 single-request on gaia-backend — harden
  the resolver without overriding dns: (which would break compose
  service discovery for postgres/redis/etc).
- DNS errors ("no such host") reclassified transient, not permanent, so
  bootstrap retries instead of giving up.
- Bump default attempts to 20 (fast backoff, cap 15s); non-blocking, so
  long convergence is harmless and self-heals.

* fix(api): daemonize juicefs mount + poll readiness (don't trust exit code)

juicefs mount enforces a ~10s mountpoint-ready check via its watchdog
parent even in foreground — under Neon meta latency it always trips, and
foreground mode then kills the child so the mount never completes
(deterministic "mount point is not ready"). With --background the parent
self-exits non-zero after the same check but the detached child finishes
the mount seconds later.

Revert to --background and ignore the invocation's exit code; supervise
the real mountpoint by polling for JUICEFS_MOUNT_READY_TIMEOUT, classify
from stderr only if it never converges. Drops the dead foreground Popen
machinery.

* security+perf(workspace): subdir-isolated JuiceFS, fused session bootstrap, fs metrics

Three threads, one PR because they cross-cut the storage + sandbox lifecycle:

1. SECURITY (critical) — per-user JuiceFS namespace isolation.
   Previous mount.sh exposed the full cross-user namespace at /mnt/jfs and
   leaked JFS_META_URL + R2 creds as sandbox-wide env vars. Any sandbox user
   could `ls /mnt/jfs/users/` to enumerate, then read/write every other
   user's session FS. Fixed by:
   - mount.sh uses `juicefs mount --subdir /users/$USER_ID` so the FUSE-
     visible tree is scoped at the kernel level; a second --subdir mount
     serves the read-only skills overlay
   - lifecycle._mount_env passes credentials only as per-call envs to the
     mount.sh invocation, not as sandbox-wide env — user shells no longer
     see them in /proc/self/environ
   - lifecycle._seed_user_subtrees pre-creates per-user dirs host-side, so
     we never need a brief admin mount of the full namespace inside the
     sandbox
   Residual risk (passwordless sudo + /proc disclosure) documented in the
   audit doc as the next follow-up.

2. PERF + OBSERVABILITY — fused host-side session bootstrap, fs metrics.
   storage.bootstrap_user_session fuses what used to be three asyncio.to_thread
   hops (ensure_session_dirs + touch_last_active + materialize_integrations)
   into one. SKILL.md catalog rewrite is hash-gated against library_hash()
   + connected-set signature — steady-state turns rewrite zero files.
   storage.metrics adds a ContextVar-isolated per-op latency aggregator
   wired into every FS-shaped operation (mount, host writes, sandbox
   acquire, tool entry, watcher rescan); flushed onto the canonical wide
   event as one `fs={...}` field for LogQL split-by-op queries.

3. PERF (bash) — single-roundtrip artifact publish.
   _publish_artifacts now uses one `find -exec sh -c ... base64` to emit
   path, size, and inline body for every artifact in one stream, replacing
   the prior N+1 envd round-trips (one `find` plus one `base64` per file).

* security(sandbox): drop sudo, hide /proc, root-only mount.sh, daemon dumpable=0

Closes every credential-recovery path from the unprivileged sandbox user to
the JuiceFS daemon's secrets (meta-DB URL, META_PASSWORD, R2 keys):

* Template (`build_e2b_template.py`) strips the sandbox user from `sudo` and
  `wheel` groups, purges NOPASSWD rules under `/etc/sudoers.d/`, and live-
  remounts `/proc` with `hidepid=invisible` so PID enumeration of root-owned
  processes is denied. Pre-bakes ~12 common CLI tools so agents don't need
  `sudo apt install` at runtime.
* New `jfs_launcher.py` execs `juicefs` after `PR_SET_DUMPABLE(0)`, which
  ownership-stamps `/proc/<pid>/{environ,cmdline}` to `root:0` and refuses
  ptrace from non-CAP_SYS_PTRACE readers. Defense-in-depth even if the sudo
  strip is ever regressed.
* `mount.sh` is mode 0750 root:root; `commands.run(MOUNT_SCRIPT_PATH,
  user="root", envs=...)` runs it via e2b envd directly (no sudo
  intermediate shell), so credentials never cross an unprivileged process'
  environ. Splits the Postgres password out of the meta URL into
  `META_PASSWORD` env so it never appears in the daemon's argv.
* Sandbox writes (`bash` tool, `acquire_sandbox`) go through `user="root"`
  for the handful of root-needing ops; the bash tool itself stays
  unprivileged. The accesslog tail (`artifact_watcher`) reads
  `/mnt/jfs/.accesslog` as root since the mount is root-owned.
* `/workspace` and `/mnt/jfs` are mode 0750 owned by `user`; only the
  daemon (which holds the JuiceFS keys) can see the JuiceFS-internal paths.
* Path safety: `ensure_safe_path_id` (storage/juicefs) plus a Pydantic
  `SafePathId` constraint on `conversation_id` reject anything outside
  `[A-Za-z0-9_-]{1,64}`. File-upload endpoint also confirms ownership of the
  target conversation in Mongo before letting the write through.
* Adds `verify_sandbox_hardening.sh` as a post-template-rebuild smoke test
  and documents the model in `apps/api/CLAUDE.md`.

* security(sandbox): purge sudo binary, drop verify script from template

Followup hardening based on a live adversarial probe (drove the bash tool
as the unprivileged user, exhausted every cred-read path). The probe came
back clean — no `JFS_*`, `R2_*`, `META_PASSWORD`, or `AWS_*` leaked
through `/proc/<pid>/{environ,cmdline}`, `/mnt/jfs/.accesslog`,
`/etc/gaia/`, `mount` metadata, `env`, FS scans, FUSE internals, network
sockets, or any persisted log. Two surface-area refinements:

* **`sudo` removed entirely.** Even though Wall 1 already denied use
  (no password, no NOPASSWD rule), the setuid binary itself was sitting
  in `/usr/bin/`. Now: `apt-get purge -y sudo && autoremove` at template
  build time. `command -v sudo` returns nothing, `/etc/sudoers{,.d}` are
  gone with the package. Verify script's Wall 1 updated to accept the
  binary-absent state as PASS.

* **`verify_sandbox_hardening.sh` is no longer baked into the template.**
  Switched to push-on-demand delivery: API uploads via
  `sbx.files.write("/tmp/verify.sh", ...)`, runs, then `sbx.files.remove`.
  Keeps the sandbox surface minimal (only `mount.sh` + `jfs_launcher.py`
  in `/etc/gaia/`). The script source still ships in the repo under
  `scripts/`. Header documents the new delivery contract.

Build still completes in ~25s; the final probe re-confirmed 7/7 walls
hold via push-on-demand verify, plus zero credential leaks across 35+
read paths.

* hardening(sandbox): warn on missing SANDBOX_USER, pin skills bind ro

Two defense-in-depth tweaks surfaced by the security audit:

- If SANDBOX_USER does not exist at acquire time, the sudo-strip block
  silently no-ops. Sudo binary is purged in the template so this never
  yields privilege, but the strip becoming inert deserves a loud signal.
  Emit a WARN on stderr; lifecycle._run_mount_script already surfaces
  stderr to the API logs.

- mount --bind ... -o ro on the skills overlay is honored only on newer
  kernels; older kernels silently ignore -o ro on a bind. Add an explicit
  remount,bind,ro after the bind. The underlying FUSE is --read-only so
  writes were already rejected, but pinning the bind itself ro makes the
  read-only surface consistent at every layer.

* feat(metrics): FS_OPS Prometheus collectors + FS Ops Grafana dashboard

Collectors (all on the default registry, cross-registered onto the
worker's custom registry so both /metrics endpoints serve them):
- fs_op_duration_seconds  Histogram(operation, mode, status) — buckets
  tuned for the actual op range (sub-ms lock waits through 60s mount
  timeouts), narrower than the worker's arq_task_* buckets.
- fs_op_bytes_total       Counter(operation) — payload size for writes
  and uploads.
- fs_op_total             Counter(operation, mode, status) — lifetime
  count that never decays; backs the dashboard's lifetime totals table.
- fs_op_last_seen_unix_seconds Gauge(operation) — wall-clock of latest
  observation; renders as "5m ago" in the dashboard.
- fs_op_in_flight         Gauge(operation) — incremented in fs_timer
  enter, decremented in finally; exposes contention + stuck ops.
- sandbox_pool_size       Gauge(kind, shard) — set by SandboxPool on
  put/evict; kind=warm seeded to 0 at construction so the panel renders
  zero instead of "No data" until the warm pool capability lands.
- tool_bash_exit_code_total Counter(exit_code) — bucketed into 0 /
  1-126 / 127 / 128-254 / 255 / timeout, set after every commands.run.

- record_fs_op + add_fs_bytes wrap Prometheus emits in try/except so a
  registry bug never breaks the wide_event flush.
- fs_timer's in-flight inc/dec is crash-safe via try/finally.
- app_factory eager-imports the metrics module so /metrics surfaces the
  collector metadata lines on first scrape instead of waiting for the
  first FS op to lazy-import the storage package.
- _BASH_EXIT_CODE_TOTAL handles asyncio.TimeoutError, CancelledError,
  and SDK-specific timeout exceptions by name; non-timeout exceptions
  bucket as 255 since we can't read an exit code from a thrown call.

Grafana FS Ops dashboard (provisioned via filesystem):
- Lifetime totals table at top with operation + total + errors + last
  seen columns; always populated once any op has fired.
- In-flight ops + sandbox pool size gauges (never empty after first
  observation).

  populated through normal idle gaps.
- Error rate + byte throughput + sbx_acquire-by-mode panels wrapped in
  `or vector(0)` so quiet panels render a flat zero line instead of
  "No data".
- Bash exit code donut over [1h].
- Default range widened to now-1h; refresh 10s.
- v1 dashboard saved as fs-ops-v1.json.bak for one-release rollback.

Cardinality: ~25 ops * 5 modes * 2 statuses + 16 pool size series + 6

endpoints, no new dependencies (prometheus_client + Gauge already

## Phase 1 amendment — active banner-grab phase in sweep service

This amendment adds an opt-in active banner-grab phase to the
existing **sweep service** (`go/pkg/scan/`, NOT the SNMP/API-focused
mapper at `go/pkg/mapper/`). The phase runs after the SYN half-open
scanner identifies live `(host, port)` pairs and emits
`BannerObservation` records that the agent forwards to netprobe in
bounded batches over a new `MatchBanners` IPC method. Netprobe matches
the supplied observations against the §32 Recog / Satori corpora and
returns labels; the agent emits or forwards the resulting
`FingerprintEvent`s. No corpus duplication, no shared Rust/Go crate, no
cgo. Banner grab is a streaming enrichment pipeline over SYN-confirmed
open ports, not a second in-memory scanner; preserve the SYN half-open
scanner's large-inventory latency profile while allowing exhaustive
active probing when operators choose that trade-off. HTTPS/TLS evidence
stays in the passive TLS/SSL fingerprint pipeline rather than active
HTTPS decryption. See `design.md` D16 for the architectural rationale.

  footer hints. Mirrors confirm's overlay options.
